title: The trans/cis ratio of formic (HCOOH) and thioformic (HC(O)SH) acids in the interstellar medium
question: Whether the prevalence of one isomer over the other for formic acid (HCOOH) and thioformic acid (HC(O)SH) in the interstellar medium is due to a cis-trans isomerization transformation via quantum tunneling, and how predicted ratios compare with ALMA observations toward G31.41+0.31.

recipe.goal: Compute ab initio electronic structures and energies for cis, trans, and transition state geometries of HCOOH and HC(O)SH
recipe.method: Unconstrained geometry optimization and frequency calculation at B2PLYP-D3(BJ)/aug-cc-pVTZ level, followed by single-point energy correction with CCSD(T)-F12 and anharmonic ZPE correction via second-order vibrational perturbative theory; orbital interactions studied via second-order perturbation theory and solvation test in water with SMD.
key_parameters: Basis sets: aug-cc-pVTZ for B2PLYP-D3(BJ); cc-pVTZ-F12-CABS, cc-pVTZ-F12, and aug-cc-pVQZ for CCSD(T)-F12

recipe.goal: Calculate unimolecular cis-trans isomerization rate constants and equilibrium ratios across 10-400 K
recipe.method: Canonical variational transition state theory (CVT) with multidimensional small curvature tunneling (SCT) approximation; minimum energy path (MEP) energies corrected with CCSD(T)-F12 using interpolated single-point energies (ISPE) algorithm.
key_parameters: Temperature range T = 10-400 K; ZPE scaling factors 0.948 for HCOOH and 0.949 for HC(O)SH
assumptions: High-frequency anharmonicities accounted for via constant ZPE scaling factor along reaction path

recipe.goal: Identify transitions and derive column densities, abundances, and trans/cis ratios of HCOOH and HC(O)SH toward G31.41+0.31
recipe.method: Synthetic LTE spectrum generation and automated line fitting using SLIM and MADCUBA-AUTOFIT on the GUAPOS 3mm spectrum, accounting for line opacity and contamination from all previously modeled species in the survey.
key_parameters: Four LTE parameters: column density (N), excitation temperature (T_ex), peak radial velocity (v_LSR), and FWHM; for t-HCOOH, v_LSR fixed to 96.5 km s^-1; for c-HCOOH, t-HC(O)SH, and c-HC(O)SH, T_ex = 152 K, v_LSR = 96.5 km s^-1, and FWHM = 8.0 km s^-1 fixed to t-HCOOH values
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), justified by high volume density n(H2) ~ 10^8 cm^-3; H2 column density N_H2 = (1.0 +/- 0.2) x 10^25 cm^-2; distance 3.75 kpc

score_reason: Quantum chemical and kinetic methods, software versions, basis sets, scaling factors, and target transitions (Table 2) are thoroughly documented, and the ALMA project code is provided. However, reproducing the spectral fits requires the pre-reduced GUAPOS 1D spectrum and the multi-species background LTE model from companion papers (Mininni et al. 2020; Colzi et al. 2021).
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA dataset (2017.1.00501.S) is public, the exact fitted transitions and frequencies are listed in Table 2, and the main observational and theoretical outputs are clear numeric values (column densities, T_ex, FWHM, rate constants, and trans/cis ratios).
